title: Voice qualification evidence: the bridge's receipts, the principal's read, and the grant on the assignment and room token
why: Pack 03 G7 drives a synthetic in-app voice episode from the Voice Lab. The browser sends Opus over WebRTC to LiveKit and the media bridge talks to the provider on the server, so the Lab needs product-authored receipts for the legs only the product sees (docs/plans/voice-qualification-g7.md, sophia.voice-qualification.v1).

Off by default, three times over: migration 0046's grant is the migration owner's alone; the API serves none of this unless SOPHIA_VOICE_QUALIFICATION=on (off, it passes no grant on, runs no guard and needs nothing of 0046 to be ready); and the bridge records nothing unless SOPHIA_VOICE_EVIDENCE=on and its assignment names a grant (qualification, omitted otherwise). A room token names the grant only for its principal while it is active.

No speech is retained: every receipt schema allows only numbers, booleans, enumerated words, ids, hex digests and times; no free text. Receipts are kept 24 hours and only the grant's principal reads them; anyone else finds nothing (not_found, 422, as the API's other reads).

The guard (0046) runs on every presence report and assignment poll, and every evidence write and reservation checks the same limits for its own exchange, so an exchange under a grant ends at its deadline or limit whether or not the Lab is still there.

Joins the Lab needs to prove a run's outcome and its cleanup, all only with voice qualification on: a native task names the exchange whose voice tool call created it (exchangeId); a member reads their own voice tool calls in an exchange, in order, each with the command it admitted and the task that command created (getExchangeCalls), so a step is proven by the call that made it, never by a key, a time window or another call; and a member reads the room as the bridge last saw it, only whether they are in it and the counts (getRoomLivePresence). A call's command is linked to it by the transaction that inserted that command for the call, never by its key, so a member's own command, under any key, links to no call.

The bound is the exchange's, held by the service, never a bridge session's: before the bridge opens a provider connection under a grant or lets a generation start, it reserves it (POST /v1/media/qualification-reserve), and the service counts connections and generations durably, with what each connection was charged and reported. A session that replaces a lost one, or a restarted bridge, starts from the exchange's true counts. A reservation that does not fit ends the exchange, as does the bridge's own stop (a session_closed receipt that says guard: reason bridge). A receipt names only a connection that was reserved.

What a withdrawal reached, only with voice qualification on: a research, design or review task's detail lists the sources its attempt drew on that are withdrawn now (withdrawnSourceIds), from the very closure a withdrawal revokes work by, computed live. The Lab matches a forgotten mission note's sourceId (its record_note receipt's) against it. A task that had already ended lists it too, so the Lab also reads that the task was live just before its withdrawal.

value.description: The operator grant an exchange is under (sophia.voice-qualification.v1, migration 0046), while it is active: the bridge records receipts only then, and only while principalActorId holds the floor. Omitted for every other exchange.
Present only for the grant's principal while the grant is active: the Studio then emits its page receipts (sophia:voice-qualification) to that page alone. Never stored.

From the first 16 kHz chunk the bridge forwarded to the provider for the principal until the turn completes, is interrupted, hands off, pauses or closes. pcmSha256Chain covers the PCM forwarded (sha-256-chain-v1); it is never comparable to the Lab's source audio. connection is the durable ordinal its connection's reservation returned.
The provider's turn for an input window ended. transcriptChars is a count only: no transcript is kept.

The provider session's lifecycle and usage, on one reserved connection (connection is the durable ordinal its reservation returned). usageTokens and lastPromptTokens are that connection's own: what the provider reported of its session, which the service keeps as the connection's highest report. connectionsOpened and turns are what the bridge saw; the service's own counts are the reservations'.

A reply the bridge played to the room ended. playedSha256Chain covers the 20 ms frames handed to the room track (sha-256-chain-v1). connection is the durable ordinal its connection's reservation returned.
The bridge's session for the exchange closed. transcriptRetained is always false.

One bridge receipt for an exchange under a grant, by its per-exchange sequence number: the same receipt again is a no-op, another under the same number is refused (409 idempotency_conflict). Only numbers, booleans, enumerated words, ids, digests and times: no free text.
Whether the exchange has ended, and why (null when it has not): a guard reason, or bridge when the bridge's own bound or the deadline stopped its session (its session_closed receipt said guard).

The bridge's durable reservation for an exchange under a grant, before it spends: a provider connection before it opens one; a generation before it sends what can start one (input after a turn ended, a tool response, a notice, a typed message), on a reserved connection; or a generation that started unasked (its output arrived), which is counted and charged whatever the limits. charge is the generation's worst case (the context again and its output twice) plus what was sent and transcribed since the connection's last charge. Or the bridge's own stop (stop: its bound or the deadline stopped the session, whoever holds the floor): it reserves and records nothing, and the exchange ends (reason bridge), once; an exchange already ended answers it the same (ok, ended).
Granted, with a connection's durable ordinal (null for a generation), or refused: then the exchange has ended (ended true) and stop says why.
Written by the service when its guard ended the exchange (seq 0).

What the grant's principal may read of an exchange its grant covers: the grant's limits and what was reserved and reported against them, and the receipts kept (24 hours) in order. Anyone else finds nothing.

connectionsOpened.description: Provider connections reserved for the exchange (durable: only a reservation adds to it).

turns.description: Generations reserved for the exchange, asked for or not (durable: only a reservation adds to it).

usageTokens.description: What the provider reported, each reserved connection's highest report, summed.

committedTokens.description: What the exchange may have cost: each reserved connection at the greater of what was charged to it (each generation at its worst case) and what the provider reported of it, summed. The guard holds this to the budget.

lastPromptTokens.description: The prompt size the exchange's latest connection last reported.

value.description: The room as the media bridge last saw it, for a member: whether the caller is in it, how many people are and how many of them are guests, the bridge's voice and the report's age. Nobody else's identity. observed false (no report) or fresh false (older than 15 s; the bridge reports every 5 s while it is in the room) proves nothing either way.

A member's own voice tool calls in an exchange, in the order the service recorded them (seq, increasing across all exchanges), each with the tool it named, the command it admitted, the task that command created, and when and how the API answered it. Only calls of a voice qualification grant's principal, in an exchange opened under that grant, are recorded. command is null for a call that admitted nothing (a read, a clarification, a refusal: a Hold on work that is not running admits no command; a repeat answered with the task under way) and for one not answered yet (answeredAt null: whatever it admits may not have committed). A replayed call is its first call's one entry. A command is the call's only when the transaction that inserted it did so for this call; a member's own command under the call's key is not. Another member's calls and another exchange's are never listed. readAt is when this was read: given back as after, only calls whose recording began after that read are listed, so a call already on its way at that read, committed or not, never is.

The exchange whose voice tool call created the task: the call the service recorded when it bound the call to its speaker, to which the task's command was linked by the transaction that inserted it for that call (0046, live_tool_calls). The canonical join from a voice step to its task, and through it to the task's output. Omitted for any other task, and for one created while the API's voice qualification was off. A member's own command, under any idempotency key, never sets it.

The sources this research, design or review task drew on that are withdrawn now, in order: its attempt's consumed closure (its manifest and everything that drew on, transitively; for a design or an edit, the report version it lays out and so the research that wrote it and that research's inputs, a mission note's version among them), the closure a withdrawal revokes work by, less what is still an eligible, ready project source (0046, task_withdrawn_sources). Computed live, never stored: a task that ended before a withdrawal lists it as well, so it proves what the task drew on, not what ended it. Omitted for any other kind of task, and by an API with voice qualification off.

post.summary: The bridge's receipt for an exchange under a voice qualification grant. Served only by an API with voice qualification on (SOPHIA_VOICE_QUALIFICATION=on); the bridge sends receipts only with SOPHIA_VOICE_EVIDENCE=on and an assignment that names the grant. The guard runs in the same transaction and may end the exchange.

200.description: Recorded, or the same receipt again

403.description: The exchange is not under this grant

409.description: Another receipt holds this sequence number (idempotency_conflict)

422.description: Request fails the declared schema, or the receipt is not bound to this grant and run

post.summary: The bridge's durable reservation of a provider connection or a generation for an exchange under a voice qualification grant, under the exchange's lock. A reservation that does not fit ends the exchange. Served only by an API with voice qualification on (SOPHIA_VOICE_QUALIFICATION=on).

200.description: Granted, or refused and the exchange ended

403.description: The exchange is not under this grant

422.description: Request fails the declared schema, the exchange is not found (not_found), or a generation names a connection that was not reserved

get.summary: The grant's principal reads what was recorded of an exchange its voice qualification grant covers: the grant's limits, what was reported against them, why the guard ended it, and the receipts kept. Served only by an API with voice qualification on. Read-only; anyone else, or an exchange under no grant, is not found.

422.description: Not the grant's principal, or no grant covers the exchange (not_found)

get.summary: A member reads the room as the media bridge last saw it: whether they themselves are in it, the counts, the bridge's voice and the report's age; nobody else's identity. Served only by an API with voice qualification on. A room outside the caller's projects is not found.

422.description: Not a room of the caller's projects (not_found)

get.summary: A member reads their own voice tool calls in an exchange, in the order they were recorded, each with its tool, the command it admitted, the task that command created and how it was answered. With after (an earlier read's readAt), only calls whose recording began after that read. Served only by an API with voice qualification on. An exchange outside the caller's projects is not found.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: An earlier read's readAt: only calls whose recording began after it.

200.description: The caller's calls in the exchange

422.description: Not an exchange of the caller's projects (not_found)
